newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Thursday on short-covering, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,375 yuan ($407) per tonne, rising five yuan. It opened at 3,370 and hit a low of 3,350 yuan per tonne.
July rose eight yuan to 3,213, September gained 31 to 3,331, the January 1998 contract fell three yaun to 3,313, March was unchanged at 3,365 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 17,100 tonnes from 19,200 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly higher and moved at high levels for most of the session, traders said.

"Short-covering by retail investors was responsible for today's gains," one trader said. "But a lack of market-moving news is likely to lead to liquidation of long-term positions in the next few days, depressing prices."
Traders said they expected soybeans to meet strong selling pressure at high levels in the short term.
